e7_s4_rationale: The patient's history of laparoscopic appendectomy 8 months earlier and the presence of a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole with a pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips on the CT scan are consistent with appendiceal stump appendicitis, which is an inflammation of the appendiceal stump remaining after an appendectomy.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Pericecal abscess
e7_s4_rejected.why: While the patient has a pericecal collection, the presence of a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole suggests a more specific diagnosis related to the appendiceal stump.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Cecal diverticulitis
e7_s4_rejected.why: There is no mention of a cecal diverticulum in the CT scan findings, making this diagnosis less likely.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Typhlitis
e7_s4_rejected.why: Typhlitis typically occurs in the context of neutropenia or immunocompromised states, which are not mentioned in the patient's history.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Chronic appendiceal abscess
e7_s4_rejected.why: The acute presentation and lack of chronic symptoms make this diagnosis less likely compared to appendiceal stump appendicitis.
